newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Horse Racing-Bailey names O'Dwyer as stable jockey.
newsitem.headline: Horse Racing-Bailey names O'Dwyer as stable jockey.

text.p: Newbury-based handler Kim Bailey said on Wednesday that he had secured the services of Gold Cup-winning rider Conor O'Dwyer as his new stable jockey.
Bailey has signed the Irishman as a replacement for Norman Williamson who left the yard to ride as a freelance in the summer.
"I am very pleased as Conor is a top jockey and has been at the top for a long time," the trainer said. "He will have his first ride for me at Uttoxeter on Saturday."
Despite his new job, O'Dwyer will maintain his partnership with Imperial Call, who gave him the biggest success of his career in the Gold Cup at Cheltenham last March.
"He will still be going back and forward to Ireland," Bailey explained.
"He has still got his own contacts in Ireland and won't be with me the whole time but they tend to race mainly on the weekend over there so he should be able to do both."
Bailey also trains the 1995 Gold Cup winner Master Oats but hopes to avoid a battle over O'Dwyer's services for next year's blue riband of chasing.
"The chances are that Master Oats will be going for the Grand National this season so we should be OK," he said.
